chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim and Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from him who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Prophets and the Messengers are upon four categories. There is a Prophet who is informed within himself, without going beyond others; and there is a Prophet who sees in sleep and hears the voice, and does not see him (the angel) while awake, and was not sent to anyone, and upon him is an Imam — similar to how Ibrahim was above Lot (peace be upon him).
And there is a Prophet who sees in his sleep and hears the voice and sees the Angel face to face, and has been sent to a group, be they few or many, like Yunus —
God said to Yunus: 'And We sent him to a hundred thousand, or more' [37:147]
He said: 'The "or more" refers to thirty thousand,' and upon him is an Imam. And the one who sees in his sleep and hears the voice and sees while awake — he is an Imam, like the Uli al-'Azm.
And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was indeed a Prophet but not an Imam, until God said:
'I am making you an Imam for the people.' He (Ibrahim) said: 'And from my offspring?' God said: 'My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.' [2:124]
Whoever worshipped an idol or a graven image cannot be an Imam.

key_terms.أُولُو الْعَزْمِ: Prophets of firm resolve — the five greatest prophets: Noah, Ibrahim, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad
key_terms.اليقظة: Wakefulness, the state of being awake (contrasted with dreams)
key_terms.مُنَبَّأ: Informed one, one who receives prophetic information
key_terms.يُعَايِن: To see face-to-face, to witness directly

ai.seo_question: What are the four categories of Prophets and Messengers according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) describes the four hierarchical categories of prophets and messengers, distinguishing between those who receive revelation privately, those sent to limited communities, and the highest rank — the Uli al-'Azm (Prophets of firm resolve) who are simultaneously Imams. The hadith crucially establishes that prophethood and imamate are distinct offices: Ibrahim (AS) was a prophet before being elevated to the rank of Imam, and God's covenant of imamate explicitly excludes those who engaged in idol worship. This teaching contextualizes the Shia doctrine that the Imamate is the highest spiritual and political station, superior to general prophethood.
